subject: subjunc: much fewer junctions detected compare to STAR aligner?

messages.author: e6a8fbaffd0c1045
messages.subject: subjunc: much fewer junctions detected compare to STAR aligner?
parts:
Hello subread developers,

On the same raw data, subjunc reports about 100k junctions, whereas STAR reports about 1 million junctions. I assisted STAR run  with GTF file from rat genome. Is it alright to have this low number of junction? If not, how do I improve it?

Kind regards
Vang

messages.author: 6569f7247d312021
messages.subject: Re: subjunc: much fewer junctions detected compare to STAR aligner?
parts:
Hi Vang,

Given that your dataset is a DNA sequencing dataset, it would be really a surprise to me if there are a million breakpoints in your data. You may have a close look at a few reported breakpoints in IGB/IGV to see if they are possibly just mapping errors.

Cheers,
Wei

messages.author: e6a8fbaffd0c1045
messages.subject: Re: subjunc: much fewer junctions detected compare to STAR aligner?
parts:

I ran RNA-seq data this time. Anyway, I will check the some of the breakpoints as you suggested when I have access to my data.

Cheers
